title: Getting Started with JavaScript
description: Introduction to variables, data types, and operators.

lessons.title: What is JavaScript?
lessons.content: JavaScript is a powerful, versatile programming language primarily used for enhancing web pages by making them interactive and dynamic. It allows developers to manipulate webpage content, handle user events, and communicate with servers without needing to reload the page.

lessons.title: JavaScript in the Browser
lessons.content: Within web browsers, JavaScript acts as the engine that drives user interaction. It interacts with the Document Object Model (DOM) to dynamically change the content, style, and structure of web pages in response to user actions such as clicks, typing, and navigation.

lessons.title: Variables in JavaScript
lessons.content: Variables in JavaScript serve as named containers that store data values. These can hold different types of data and are essential for writing flexible and maintainable code. Modern JavaScript encourages the use of `let` and `const` for variable declarations due to their block scope and immutability features.

lessons.title: Declaring Variables
lessons.content:
/* Declaring variables using let, const, and var */
let age = 30; // age can be reassigned
const name = 'Alice'; // name cannot be changed
var isStudent = true; // var is function-scoped and less recommended

lessons.title: Data Types Overview
lessons.content: JavaScript includes several primitive data types: String for text, Number for numeric values, Boolean for true/false, Null representing intentional absence of any object value, Undefined for uninitialized variables, and Symbol for unique identifiers. Understanding these is critical to managing data effectively.

Comments in JavaScript
lessons.content: Comments are essential for documenting your code and explaining complex logic. Single-line comments start with `//`, while multi-line comments are wrapped inside `/* */`. Comments are ignored during code execution.

lessons.title: Basic Operators
lessons.content: JavaScript provides a variety of operators to perform computations and assignments. Arithmetic operators include addition (+), subtraction (-), multiplication (*), and division (/). Assignment operators like = assign values to variables, enabling dynamic data manipulation.
